archetype.name: Game Manager (veteran backup)
archetype.definition: A short-area, on-schedule passer who keeps the ball out of harm's way and completes what the play design gives him, but rarely pushes it downfield and doesn't create on his own.

report.headline: Accurate, careful, and now fourth on the depth chart
report.take:
Gardner Minshew is what he has been for eight seasons: a timing-and-rhythm passer who gets the ball out around 2.5 seconds, throws short of the sticks, and lives on completion percentage. His 10.15 CPOE leads all 55 qualifiers and his 7.5% bad-throw rate ranks second, so the accuracy is real. The career shows he has always sat near league average in overall efficiency, though, and his intended air yards (6.98) and aggressiveness (7.55%) are low even by his own standards. He completes what's open and doesn't go looking for more.

The season line is really two very different games. In Week 8 he came on in relief against Dallas, played 42% of the snaps, threw three touchdowns and added 13.2 EPA. That came against a defense that now ranks 32nd. His one start, at Seattle (6th), was a 3-17 loss: -5.1 EPA, three sacks, no touchdowns, and -0.155 EPA per dropback. That start, not the blended +0.141, is the better guide to what he gives a struggling offense against a competent defense.

The small samples flatter a few things. Most of his EPA came on seven intermediate throws (1.379 EPA per play, two TDs) and five fourth-quarter close-game snaps, which is far too little to bank. Under the surface, his eight deep attempts produced a 37.5% completion rate and negative EPA, third downs were a losing proposition (35.7% conversions), and he took sacks on 44.4% of pressures, 43rd of 45. That last one isn't new: he has always taken sacks under pressure rather than throwing the ball away or escaping.

Where it's heading is mostly a roster question. Arizona started Josh Johnson in Week 11, and as of Nov. 24 Minshew is listed fourth at quarterback even with Carson Beck out with back spasms. Unless that changes, the most likely rest-of-season line for him is a clipboard. If he is pressed back into duty, expect tidy completion numbers, modest yardage, and an offense that stalls against good fronts.

strengths.title: Accuracy on the throws he takes
strengths.body: He leads qualifiers in CPOE and has the second-lowest bad-throw rate, and he completed 84.6% on short throws with positive EPA. This follows from his style: quick, defined reads to the first open man. It has held up in his better career seasons (2020, 2021), so it's a stable trait. Its limit is that the throws are short.

strengths.title: No giveaways so far
strengths.body: Zero interceptions on 53 attempts, and no lost fumbles. Part of that is design, since a low-aggressiveness passer avoids risky windows. Part of it is sample size: he threw 9 and 10 picks in his 2023 and 2024 seasons, so the clean sheet will not hold over real volume.

strengths.title: Finds Wilson and McBride
strengths.body: Michael Wilson (0.628 EPA per target) and Trey McBride (0.338) account for most of the passing value. Middle-of-the-field throws were his best area, with 91.7% completions. Feeding two reliable targets between the numbers suits how he plays.

concerns.title: The good game came against the worst defense
concerns.body: His +13.2 EPA relief outing came against Dallas, now the 32nd-ranked defense. His only start, against 6th-ranked Seattle, went negative. With two games of evidence, the opponent explains more of the gap than anything he changed. The starter line is the sober read.

concerns.title: Pressure turns into sacks
concerns.body: He was pressured on only 15.8% of dropbacks, but 44.4% of those pressures ended in sacks, 43rd of 45. Seattle sacked him three times on a 9.1% starter sack rate. He has posted mid-to-high pressure-to-sack rates for years, so this is a trait, not noise. It's costly behind a line now missing guard Jon Gaines.

concerns.title: Little downfield or on third down
concerns.body: Deep throws went 37.5% with negative EPA, and third downs were a net loss with a 35.7% conversion rate. Living short of the sticks (-1.45 air yards to sticks) shows up most when the offense needs a chunk play. The eight-throw deep sample is thin, but it matches a career of modest aDOTs.

trend.note: A sharp relief outing against Dallas gave way to a flat start at Seattle. Arizona then turned to Josh Johnson in Week 11 and has dropped Minshew to fourth on the depth chart.

nextGame.headline: Friendly pass defense, but he's unlikely to see the field
nextGame.body:
On paper Washington suits a short-passing quarterback. It allows 282.3 yards a game to quarterbacks (31st) and pushes offenses to throw (3rd-strongest pass funnel). It also generates little pressure, with a 26th-ranked sack rate, which hides his worst habit. Arizona is a 7.5-point home underdog with a 40.5 total. The Cardinals' 32nd-ranked pass defense points to a trailing, pass-heavy script, and that's where his volume came from this year.

Availability decides everything. Carson Beck is out with back spasms, yet Minshew is still listed QB4 behind Johnson and others, so the base case is no snaps. Guard Jon Gaines (ankle) is out and RB Jeremiyah Love remains on IR. On Washington's side, starting corner Amik Robertson (98% of snaps) missed Monday's game with an ankle injury, which would loosen coverage for whoever does throw.

keyMatchups.title: McBride against a soft TE defense
keyMatchups.body: Washington ranks last in letting lead tight ends outscore their averages. McBride was one of Minshew's two most productive targets. If Minshew plays, the middle-of-field throws to McBride are the cleanest path to production.

keyMatchups.title: Light rush meets a sack-prone passer
keyMatchups.body: Washington's 26th-ranked sack rate is about the best a quarterback with his pressure-to-sack habit can hope for. It eases the cost of Gaines being out.

keyMatchups.title: Trailing script means volume
keyMatchups.body: Arizona's pass defense ranks 32nd and the Cardinals are 7.5-point underdogs. More than half his dropbacks came trailing by nine or more, and that script is likely again.

nextGame.watch: Whether the depth chart changes with Beck out. Unless Minshew climbs from QB4, the matchup is irrelevant to him.

restOfSeason.body:
The likeliest outcome is that he doesn't throw another meaningful pass. Arizona has moved past him to Johnson and lists him fourth. If injuries push him back in, expect the Seattle version more than the Dallas one. The completion rate and low bad-throw rate should hold, because that's who he is. The touchdown rate, the intermediate efficiency, and the zero interceptions all rest on a handful of throws and should come back toward his career norms. Sacks will keep stalling drives.

The projections below apply only to games he starts. As a starter, think roughly 160-215 passing yards, under 1.5 touchdowns, and two to three sacks against average fronts. Weak pass defenses and trailing scripts are where the yardage climbs.
swingFactors: Whether Arizona moves him back up from QB4
Carson Beck's back and Josh Johnson's play
Health of the interior line with Gaines out

confidence.note: Two games, one start, and a role that has shrunk to fourth string.
